messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — 2024-06-13T07:00Z - elevated p95 latency on /v1/generate (hosted) in us-east-1. error-rate creeping up. paging on-call. auto-run diagnostics started. :rotating_light:

sara: i’m on it, reading the snapshot now. seeing queue depth spike on gpu-pool-1 and a cluster of IPs from a single ASN sending huge parallel requests (likely a bursty partner). free/dev-tier traffic is ~60% of the pressure.

jay: can we apply emergency global rate-limit scoped to free/dev tiers to blunt incoming pressure? suggest aggregate 10rps per pool and reduce per-account burst.

mike: +1. also we have spare capacity in us-west and eu-west. recommend smart-routing: steer premium/paid traffic away from us-east, and route dev/free to best-effort pool. will create policy canary.

elaine: quick customer-impact note: internal checks show ~18 hosted customers saw degraded latency > p95 for 2+ minutes, no full errors yet. tagging support to outreach if this persists.

sara: applying rate-limits now via control plane. command: 

```
redwoodctl rate-limits set --scope tier=free --max-rps 10 --burst 200 --window 60s --reason "emergency pressure us-east"
```

(slash output) rate-limits applied -> policy-id rl-20240613-01 :thumbsup:

jay: creating routing policy canary config (will push to 10% traffic then ramp if stable). snippet: 

```yaml
routing_policy: tiered-steering-2024-06-13
priority: 800
match:
  - tier: premium
  - route: generate
actions:
  - type: steer
    targets:
      - region: us-west-2
        weight: 80
      - region: eu-west-1
        weight: 20
fallback: us-east-legacy
```

jay: pushing canary via ops UI -> deploy-bot will report.

deploy-bot: routing update redwood-routing:tiered-steering-2024-06-13 deployed (canary 10%) across control-plane hosts.

elaine: also reducing per-account burst tokens for hosted dev/free accounts to limit token drain: 
```
redwoodctl quotas update --account-type free,dev --burst 2000 --per-minute 10000
```

elaine: disabling non-essential streaming for free tier to eliminate long-lived connections (feature flag off). 
`ffctl set streaming_free_tier false --env prod --reason "emergency mitigation"`

sara: metrics update: p95 latency (us-east) dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms within 6m of rate-limit + canary steering. request rate to gpu-pool-1 down 48%. tail still rough for small subset.

mike: good. switch to ramping steering to 50% for premium only. leave free/dev throttles until stable.

jay: ramp command: 
```
opsctl routing set-weight --policy tiered-steering-2024-06-13 --region us-west-2 --weight 50 --target premium
```

deploy-bot: canary ramp executed -> policy now at 50% for premium routes.

prod-ops-bot: Created support ticket INC-2247 and alerting blameless-runbook assigned. Affected customers: cust-alpha, cust-beta, partner-58. Support notified and templated message queued.

support-engineer: prepping customer comms: short note explaining transient latency, we throttled free/dev traffic and routed premium to alternate regions; offer temporary credits if SLA impacted.

elaine: post-mitigation checks: KV-cache hit rates stable, no regression in output quality observed for premium model variants. quantization fallback not triggered.

sara: follow-ups: 1) investigate ASN burst and block/limit at edge, 2) add auto-steering rule to move premium traffic when p95(us-east) > 500ms, 3) run load test on gpu-pool-1 to validate capacity.

mike: agree. i’ll open infra ticket to add ASN-based edge throttle and autoscale policy for gpu-pool-1. assigning to eng-infra.

jay: i’ll own backfill work to make steer-by-cost/latency policy parameterized per-customer tier (we currently have manual weights).

sara: handing off shift now — @jay you have it. summary: emergency rate-limit for free/dev applied, streaming disabled for free, per-account bursts reduced, premium traffic steered to us-west/eu-west (50% now), p95 improved to ~380-420ms. monitor for 30m then start rollback of temporary flags if stable.

mike: thanks. I’m available if anything spikes. tagging #eng-oncall and incident channel for visibility. :person-raising-hand:

support-engineer: customer comms sent for high-touch customers; monitoring responses.

prod-ops-bot: Incident INC-2247 updated: mitigation actions logged, SLA impact flagged, postmortem owner unassigned.

jay: acknowledged handoff. will watch until 11pm PT then escalate to night on-call if needed. leaving a short action list in the incident ticket.

sara: closing loop here — please copy any findings to the postmortem when you start it. thanks team. :heart:

(End of thread)
__notes: generated slack thread about live traffic mitigation and smart routing policies; flat JSON fields only
